heroHeadline: Alberta's Kenney and Smith Clash Publicly Over Using Oil as Tariff Leverage
heroSubtitle: With Canada's C$27.6B retaliation package still set to take effect Sept 8, a public rift opened within Alberta's Conservative movement: former premier Jason Kenney said Aug 28 that oil, gas and potash export taxes 'need to be on the table' as leverage against Washington, while current Premier Danielle Smith rejected an energy export tax outright, warning a 50% tariff on Canada's daily US oil exports risks losing the American market 'entirely, if not forever.' Separately, a leaked Aug 17 letter from Ontario Premier Doug Ford, reported Aug 23, revealed he had pushed PM Carney to target additional retaliatory tariffs at eight Trump-aligned US states; Ottawa did not adopt state-specific targeting in the finalized package. Markets shrugged off the latest tariffs so far, with the TSX gaining 93.89 points on Aug 24.
